briefHtml:
NAV S$10,350,927 (watcher -0.53%; listed -2.79% — stale baseline, see notes)

  • Biggest mover (Tue, verified): oil — WTI +4.2% to $105.70, Brent $108.55 on fresh Houthi strikes against Saudi (East-West pipeline still shut). In-book: Tencent +1.90% to HK$438.80 led HK; SMIC bleed slowed to -0.90% (HK$60.75, 6th down day); Xiaomi -2.43%; STI -1.39%.
  • The one thing: FOMC decides TONIGHT — statement ~2:00am SGT Thu, Warsh presser ~2:30am. CME FedWatch 95% priced for +25bp to 3.75-4.00% (first hike since Jul 2023, first under Warsh). 10y closed ~5.00% after touching 5.041% — highest since 2007. The rate is priced; the fight is guidance (money markets price >90bp of hikes over 12m).

Watcher flags: 3 critical — all stale-baseline artifacts (4th day running)

  • Verified Tuesday vs flags: SMIC -0.90% (flag -7.0%), SILJ $29.25 +0.24% (flag -7.5%), SLVP Monday $37.61 -3.84% (flag -7.6%, Tue unverified). Flags compare vs ~Sep 4-8 baselines, not Tuesday. Real cumulative drift: SMIC ~-20% from Aug 18 pivot, SILJ ~-8% from Sep 4, CDL ~-9% from Sep 4.
  • FX: USDSGD 1.2732; implied USDCNY ~6.70. priceErrors: L46.SI feed still down (4th session). navHistory reconciles +0.05% (10,345,833 → 10,350,927); watcher restated yesterday's Sep 15 NAV — standing quirk.

Insider trades (SGX/HK, 7d)

  • None found for held names Sep 9-16 (SGX Form 1/3 hits — Metrocon, AsiaPhos — are not held names; HKEX checks on Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi clean). Color: Singtel's daily S$2bn buy-back continued (filings Sep 11, 14) — issuer demand, not insider dealing. US holdings are ETFs — no insider reports exist.

Congress trades (filings Sep 10-15)

  • House Dem (NJ-5): MSFT options ~$1M two-sided (bought AND sold $250K-500K and $500K-1M, Aug 14, filed Sep 15) + small QSR/AMAT/RSG buys. House Dem (WA-1): bought $15-50K NYC muni bond.
  • Sen. King (I-ME): sold EA $15-50K (filed Sep 14). Rep. Kean (R-NJ-7): sold MSFT $15-50K + GOOGL/AMCR/JNJ small; bought LIN/MTZ (filed Sep 14).
  • Sen. Republican (AR): sold Constellation Energy $1-15K (nuclear/AI-power name), bought Otis/small-caps/2x SPY (filed Sep 11). Rep. Cisneros (D-CA-31): ~45-trade August batch — sold NVDA/TSLA/META/COIN, bought MSFT/GS/ETN/PWR (filed Sep 11). Source · BeltwayIQ w38 (still 0 — grouping lag)

Policy watch

  • FOMC tonight: 95% priced for +25bp to 3.75-4.00%, statement Thu 2:00am SGT; money markets price >90bp of hikes over 12m (LSEG); DB sees 'baby cycle'; Jefferies/First Abu Dhabi Bank urge 'keep powder dry'. Vote split + presser tone = the tradable surprise. Source
  • Bessent testimony: defended record, blamed rising bond yields on global issues — fiscal pushback as the 10y prints 19-year highs. Source
  • Iran war: fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Tuesday — WTI +4.2% $105.70, Brent $108.55; East-West pipeline still shut (3-5 wk repair est.). Oil is the Fed's wildcard. Source
  • Canada: Section 338 product additions/removals effective YESTERDAY Sep 15; import bans Sep 29. Source
  • Critical minerals: no new 48h action — Jan 14 Section 232 track (uranium, rare earths, silver; price floors; negotiations) remains the live channel; Jul 13 checkpoint passed without tariffs. KL truce to Nov 10 unchanged. Source

Risk

  • Event risk (tonight): 95% priced = rate is a formality; a surprise hold = violent relief rally (HK tech, miners, SGX property); hike + cycle guidance (>90bp priced) extends the de-rating. Guidance coin-flip — don't pre-position.
  • Margin: IBKR silver line 1,777 oz x ~$63.2 x 1.2732 ≈ S$143.0k vs ~S$56.2k loan (~1.5x; equity ~S$86.8k). Silver held $63-64 all week; hawkish-surprise flush <$60 is the level that matters.
  • Concentration/FX: ~62% of liquid book idle cash; ~35% of net worth non-SGD (USD bid on oil/hike combo).

Alpha (signals, not advice)

  • Defense sleeve (15% vs ~0%): 10y ~5.00% close, 5.041% intraday (highest since 2007); TIPS 10y real 2.60%. Post-statement ≥5% holds = start tranche build; surprise hold = stand down.
  • Silver/SLVP/SILJ (20% vs ~4%): spot $63-64 all week, miners stabilized Tue — sell-rumor-buy-news: hike + $62-64 holds = reload zone; clean break <$60 = wait.
  • HK AI (Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi): Tencent +1.9% front-running a one-and-done read; SMIC bleed slowed; US semis stabilized. One-and-done guidance = snapback (Tencent is the tell); hawkish cycle = final leg down to buy. Stagger only after the statement.

trumpWatch.title: FOMC decides tonight (Thu 2:00am SGT) — 95% priced hike; guidance is the fight
trumpWatch.detail: CME FedWatch 95% for +25bp to 3.75-4.00% (first hike since Jul 2023, first under Chair Warsh; presser 2:30am SGT). 10y closed ~5.00% Tuesday after touching 5.041% — highest since 2007. Money markets price >90bp of hikes over the next 12 months (LSEG); Deutsche Bank expects a 'baby cycle'; Jefferies and First Abu Dhabi Bank argue the Fed should keep its powder dry against geopolitically-fuelled inflation. Vote split and presser tone are the tradable surprise.

trumpWatch.title: Bessent defends record to Congress, blames rising yields on global issues
trumpWatch.detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent testified Tuesday as the 10y printed 19-year highs into the Fed's first hike since 2023 — the fiscal authority publicly pushing back on the bond market's verdict while Treasury buybacks of off-the-run debt run at double the usual pace.

trumpWatch.title: Iran war: fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi — WTI +4.2% to $105.70
trumpWatch.detail: New Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia Tuesday drove WTI +4.2% to $105.70 and Brent +2.7% to $108.55. The East-West pipeline (~4% of global supply, the Hormuz bypass) remains shut with 3-5-week repair estimates. Oil is now the Fed's wildcard — every $5 on crude hardens the hiking-cycle scenario.

trumpWatch.title: Canada trade war: Section 338 product additions/removals now live (Sep 15)
trumpWatch.detail: White House fact sheet: product additions and removals under the Section 338 proclamations took effect Sep 15, 2026; import bans follow Sep 29. Second supply-side price impulse now active. Kuala Lumpur Joint Arrangement unchanged: China rare-earth export-control elimination and the US-China reciprocal-tariff suspension run to Nov 10, 2026.

trumpWatch.title: Critical minerals: Section 232 negotiation track unchanged (no new 48h action)
trumpWatch.detail: The Jan 14 proclamation on processed critical minerals and derivative products (covers uranium, rare earths, silver and 60 USGS-listed minerals) keeps Commerce/USTR negotiating agreements with price floors and trade-restricting measures on the table; the 180-day checkpoint (Jul 13) passed without tariffs. No new executive action in the last 48 hours — status quo for the rare-earths/uranium themes.
